P1.evidence: No setter notes or application read back, even though the prospect said 'I'd written some of this'. The frame ran three of four parts — 'dive into what your goals are, see where you want to go, see where you're currently at, see if we can actually help' plus 'I really want to dive into what's stopping you' — with no 'what you need' element and no agreement question; he closed the frame with 'But yeah, let's just dive into it' instead of 'Does that work?'. The open question landed cleanly: 'What can we potentially help you with, Joey?'

P2.evidence: Age and height asked directly ('so 29 and how tall are you?'); weight was volunteered and only confirmed back. Work never asked about at all — the prospect volunteered the office days and the nine-hour desk sitting. Health conditions were not asked as such; the kidney disease surfaced off an injury-framed question ('anything that have came up recently or anything that you've had for a long time, stiffnesses, sorenesses'), and nothing hereditary was asked. Diet was the strongest section — 'just give an idea from what your sort of day-to-day normal eating looks like'. Sleep never asked; bedtime and 'chronic sleep deprivation' came unprompted. Energy asked, though as a leading question bundled with confidence.

P3.evidence: Aesthetics handled through a 1-10 physique scale and a six-month picture rather than the 'one thing you'd change' question. Mobility was never raised by the rep — the prospect introduced it himself during the training pillar. The bridge out of the physical was leading rather than open: 'Outside of the physical aspects... do you feel like you're being withheld confidence levels? Maybe some energy levels as well'. The deep questions were the best part of the call — 'How would that overall be for you when you've actually achieved that?' and 'how do you think that would be like the family situation?' drove properly through to marriage, kids and his father. No reflect-back reframe was ever delivered; the summaries were factual lists of goals, not 'this isn't really about the weight, it's about X'.

P4.evidence: Most of the history was volunteered in the prospect's opening monologue; the rep recapped it back ('you have done some running, been to the gym before COVID and in between, also did some calisthenics') rather than asking for it. He supplied his own answer for why calisthenics failed — 'you were cutting a lot, and that might have been the cause for becoming dizzy, right?' The root-cause questions ran well: 'what do you think is sort of in the way of already making better improvements there at the moment by yourself?' let the prospect name it himself — accountability, structure and 'I just don't know what to do'. The scripted 'the information isn't the problem' line was never used.

P5.evidence: The cost-of-inaction question ran and produced real material: 'You got busy again, you sort of let it to the side. How do you think like life would look like in six months or a year from now?' drew out weight gain, worse sleep and an older body that 'doesn't snap back'. But the willingness question was asserted rather than asked — 'Sounds like that's not something you are willing to settle for as a person, Joey' — so the prospect never had to say it. No 'why not?' and no line-in-the-sand.

P6.evidence: Belief question asked before price: 'do you feel like that's going to help you get to the goals of becoming more lean, gamifying it, gaining muscle, getting more of that confidence?'. The all-in question was never asked in its pre-price form; its equivalent only appeared after the price landed, as 'So outside of the price, would be like, yeah, I would just do it', which got 'Outside of the price, yeah, I'm fully sold'. The yes he moved forward on was explicitly conditional — 'yeah I think so if the price is right' — and rather than returning to Phase 5 he challenged it once in a single sentence and went straight to the number.

P11.evidence: No agreement was reached, so none of the payment and onboarding steps became reachable. Worth noting against the same morning's team meeting, where the rep was coached that 'you just smooth out your next steps process' and 'I don't let them get off the phone' — here the call ended with the prospect leaving to consult his wife and a WhatsApp thread as the only next step.

objection_plays.detail: The isolate move ran twice and ran well — 'is it just not doable when it comes to that amount, or do you feel like it's not worth that amount?' and 'So outside of the price, would be like, yeah, I would just do it' — producing a clean 'Outside of the price, yeah, I'm fully sold'. Nothing after that ran. No 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no open financial conversation, and none of the six financial-picture questions (cash on hand, monthly surplus, credit cards, available credit, used vs available, investments). Instead of exploring how to make $6,000 work, the rep moved the price down to a $200/month tier.

The spouse trigger was raised twice — 'I mean, I'll chat with my wife' and 'let me run my wife through all of this' — and no move from the play ran. He was not asked whether he personally felt it could get him to his goal money aside, what obstacles might come up with her, whether there was any reason she would not want him stronger, or whether this was genuinely her input versus permission to bet on himself. The rep instead granted the exit: 'If you already feel like it's a no, then that's fine.'

A cheaper functioning substitute was the real blocker and there is no scripted play for it. The prospect priced local in-person coaching at 'easily under $400 a month' and set his own band at '$200 to $300, I'd be all in'. The rep's only counters were 'why haven't you gone to someone in-person then?' and a worth question, both of which the prospect answered credibly ('I just think I could do it for less'). This is the same script gap already logged from the Badrane Hriouch call, and here it converted a $6,000 conversation into a $200/month one.

notes: Discovery was genuinely good — the consequence question and the family drive-through produced real emotional material — but the whole of Baseline around work, sleep and health conditions was left to the prospect to volunteer, and no reflect-back reframe was ever built, so there was no anchor to hold against the price. The coachable moment is the four minutes after the number: he isolated correctly, got 'outside of the price, I'm fully sold', and then discounted instead of running the money play.
